title: Pay monthly or per visit?
hook: At this month's attendance, which gym contract costs less?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Compare realized cost per visit with a pay-per-visit alternative.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Compare realized cost per visit with a pay-per-visit alternative.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: Your toy gym plan costs €72 and you visit four times. What is the realized cost per visit? Toy inputs A=[72, 4, 10]; B=[72, 8, 10].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[18, 40, 32], [9, 80, -8]]. Labels: €/visit, Pass total €, Monthly−pass €.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: The monthly price is divided by actual visits, not intended visits. The comparison case shows how a higher attendance count changes cost per visit and the comparison with day passes; it does not forecast your attendance.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Monthly €=72, Visits=8, Pass €/visit=10. What is €/visit? Answer: 9.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Monthly €=72, Visits=8, Pass €/visit=10. What is €/visit?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 9. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Gym members on monthly contracts paid over $70 a month but went about 4.3 times, roughly $17 a visit, when a $10 day pass was available (DellaVigna & Malmendier, 2006).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Compare realized cost per visit with a pay-per-visit alternative.
